forces.title: Frequent Cost and Schedule Overruns Plague Megaprojects
forces.description: Complex construction programs, including nuclear and LNG projects, commonly experience significant cost and schedule overruns, with cost overruns of about 50% being frequent. This persistent delivery challenge underscores weaknesses in execution planning and systems, impacting project profitability and stakeholder confidence and hindering successful project completion.

forces.title: Data Center and Digital Infrastructure Build-out Fuels EPC Demand
forces.description: The rapid growth in demand for computing power, driven by AI adoption, digital services, and cloud migration, is leading to unprecedented investment in data center construction. This, along with other digital infrastructure (5G networks, EV charging), provides significant new project opportunities for EPC firms involved in their design, procurement, and construction.

forces.title: Skilled Manpower Shortage Constrains Construction Timelines and Productivity
forces.description: A persistent shortage of skilled construction manpower, exacerbated by an aging workforce and retirement of seasoned employees, significantly impacts project delivery efficiency and quality consistency across various sectors like steel and data centers. This leads to reduced productivity, project delays, and challenges in attracting and retaining talent, particularly for specialized knowledge and major project experience.

forces.title: Shift to Modular, Industrialized Construction for Efficiency and Predictability
forces.description: The Indian steel industry, and construction more broadly, needs to transition from conventional, labor-intensive models to modular and industrialized execution methodologies. This involves greater adoption of modularization, standardized designs, offsite fabrication, and value engineering, which can lower manpower intensity, improve safety, compress schedules, and enhance overall project predictability by reducing timelines by 20-30%.

forces.title: Digital Technologies Revolutionize Project Monitoring and Execution
forces.description: The adoption of digital technologies like AI, IoT sensors, robotics, drones, BIM, and cloud-based construction management platforms is transforming project delivery. These tools enable real-time monitoring, progress tracking, improved coordination, asset tracking, and data-driven decision-making, addressing issues like fragmented coordination, limited on-site visibility, and inconsistent documentation, ultimately enhancing execution control, quality oversight, and predictive capabilities.

forces.title: Massive Government Capital Outlay Drives Infrastructure Development
forces.description: India's government is significantly increasing capital investment in infrastructure, including highways, railways, and urban infrastructure, with planned outlays of over US$1.7 trillion through 2030 (CRISIL). Schemes like PM Gati Shakti, the National Infrastructure Pipeline, and specific budget allocations (e.g., US$132.8 billion for infrastructure in FY27) are creating robust demand for large-scale EPC projects, accelerating growth across sectors.

forces.title: Indian Project Execution Systems Suffer from Maturity Gaps
forces.description: India's rapid capacity growth, particularly in the steel sector, has outpaced its project delivery maturity. Execution systems are yet to evolve into fully optimized, data-driven frameworks, with pronounced gaps in program strategy, procurement integration, schedule management, and project governance. This leads to schedule slippages, delayed engineering readiness, weak design-procurement alignment, and over-dependency on in-situ construction.

forces.title: Razor-Thin Margins Hinder Innovation Investment in Engineering and Construction
forces.description: The engineering and construction industry is characterized by razor-thin margins, which often limit companies' capital to invest in transformational technologies. This underinvestment can impede innovation, as evidenced by less than half of sector executives investing in basic data analytics technologies. This financial constraint poses a significant barrier to adopting advanced solutions that could improve efficiency and predictability.

forces.title: Front-Loaded Engineering Critical for Predictable Project Outcomes
forces.description: Projects that prioritize and complete a significant portion of front-end engineering before commencing construction consistently achieve smoother progress, higher contractor productivity, and tighter cost control. Conversely, executing with incomplete designs leads to rework and delays. Establishing in-house design excellence cells and integrated engineering processes is crucial for predictability and efficiency.

forces.title: Emerging Green Hydrogen and Data Center Projects Create New Opportunities
forces.description: EPC firms like Larsen & Toubro are actively developing new types of large-scale projects, such as green, AI-ready data centers and large green hydrogen plants. These emerging sectors, driven by digital transformation and energy transition mandates, represent significant new revenue streams and growth areas for Engineering, Procurement & Construction services in the medium to long term.

forces.title: Growing Private and Foreign Investment Boosts Infrastructure Projects
forces.description: Liberalized FDI rules and the establishment of an Infrastructure Finance Secretariat are attracting significant private and foreign investment into India's infrastructure sector. International investors, like Actis, are planning to double investments, enhancing capital availability. Public-private partnerships (PPPs) are also playing a crucial role, providing additional funding and accelerating project delivery across various infrastructure segments.

forces.title: Ambitious Steel Capacity Expansion Drives EPC Project Demand
forces.description: India's steel industry is undergoing an unprecedented expansion, aiming for 300 MTPA crude steel capacity by 2030, involving over INR 10 lakh crore in planned investments. This creates massive demand for large-scale capital projects, including integrated and brownfield steel plants, directly benefiting EPC firms engaged in their design, procurement, and construction.

forces.title: Concentrated EPC Capacity and Engineering Gap Limit Project Bandwidth
forces.description: India's engineering capacity is concentrated among a few firms, creating constraints during peak investment cycles. Leading EPC contractors are operating at near full order-book capacity, limiting immediate bandwidth for new large-scale projects. This engineering diversity gap, coupled with a reliance on a small pool of full-spectrum engineering firms, can lead to delays and restrict the overall pace of project delivery.

forces.title: Complex Supply Chains Hinder Decarbonization and Resilience Efforts
forces.description: The complexity of decarbonizing supply chains represents a significant obstacle to achieving net-zero targets for infrastructure and transport projects, often constituting the largest carbon footprint. Additionally, supply chain resilience is a major short-term decision influence for CEOs. These complexities pose significant challenges for EPC firms in material sourcing, logistics, and achieving environmental goals.

forces.title: Sustained Road Construction Momentum Fuels EPC Demand
forces.description: India's national highways network is expanding significantly, with a projected annual increase of 5-8% (13,000 km) in road construction momentum through 2025. This, combined with large budget allocations for the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (US$34.4 billion for FY27) and plans for Multimodal Logistics Parks, ensures a robust pipeline of road infrastructure projects for EPC contractors.

viewpoints.title: Repeatable Formula Key for Successful Megaproject Execution Amid Delivery Challenges
viewpoints.description: Bain & Company identifies five critical elements for successful nuclear and broader megaproject delivery: proven design, programmatic approach, industrialized delivery, strong owner leadership, and stakeholder alignment. Despite persistent delivery challenges and frequent cost/schedule overruns (up to 50%), success is achievable by embedding and actively managing these integrated elements early. This framework provides a repeatable formula for improving execution precision and predictability in complex capital programs.

viewpoints.title: Execution Excellence, Digital Integration Crucial for India's Steel Capacity Expansion
viewpoints.description: KPMG in India, supported by industry leaders from Jindal Stainless, ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel India, and JSW Steel, highlights the urgent need for execution excellence in India's steel sector. With significant capital investments planned, successful capacity creation (targeting 300 MTPA by 2030) depends on design standardization, modular construction, and digital integration. Addressing existing gaps in delivery maturity, engineering readiness, and skilled manpower is paramount to translating investment ambition into predictable operational capacity.

viewpoints.title: AI Crucial for Accelerating Complex Megaproject Execution and Risk Management
viewpoints.description: Zyna Boubez, Partner at KPMG in Canada, asserts that AI is a powerful enabler for accelerated project execution and improved management of escalating costs and risks in complex, multi-phased megaprojects. AI helps achieve this through process standardization, readiness validation, systematic application of lessons learned, enhanced supply-chain leverage, and unlocking economic benefits. This perspective positions AI as a transformative tool for the EPC industry, addressing predictability challenges.

viewpoints.title: India Must Adopt Industrialized Construction for Faster, Cost-Efficient Project Delivery
viewpoints.description: KPMG advocates for India to adapt China's industrialized construction approaches to significantly improve construction speed, cost efficiency, and quality outcomes. China's five-fold steel production expansion was driven by disciplined standardization, mechanization, and digital integration, reducing project delivery timelines by 20-30% compared to Indian averages. Key levers include design standardization, front-loaded engineering, integrated EPC models, modularization, and digital project controls, which India needs to selectively implement.

viewpoints.title: Front-End Engineering, Modular Design, Skilled Manpower Foundational for Project Predictability
viewpoints.description: KPMG emphasizes that predictable, high-quality project execution in India's steel sector relies fundamentally on front-end engineering readiness, adoption of modular design for modular construction, and strengthening contractor capabilities by ensuring skilled manpower. Over-reliance on external consultants can lead to delays, while internal design excellence cells offer better control. Addressing the skilled manpower shortage is also critical, requiring policy intervention and industry action for workforce well-being and retention.

viewpoints.title: Early Clarity, Value-Based Procurement, Digital Oversight Essential for Steel Project Delivery
viewpoints.description: KPMG asserts that predictable project delivery for India's steel capacity expansion begins long before construction. It requires early contracting clarity, thorough pre-construction preparedness, value-based procurement (involving OEMs/contractors early in design), and integrated logistics planning. Furthermore, robust governance with digital oversight, including KPI-linked tracking and 4D/5D dashboards, forms the backbone of predictable delivery, driving accountability and discipline to meet project timelines and budgets effectively.

viewpoints.title: India's Steel Future Hinges on Institutionalized Execution Discipline, Not Just Investment
viewpoints.description: KPMG concludes that India's journey to 300 MTPA steel capacity will be defined not merely by investment volume but by the maturity of its execution ecosystem. Success necessitates institutionalizing engineering discipline, digital oversight, value-based procurement, and workforce capability. Execution excellence must transform from an operational goal to a strategic priority across the steel value chain, requiring structured approaches between policymakers, EPC contractors, and technology providers to strengthen delivery standards and governance.
